clinical_category: COPD self-management - individualized exacerbation action plan
blueprint_topic: Client education and coordinated self-management planning for COPD exacerbations
stem: A nurse reviews an individualized COPD action plan with a client. What is the primary purpose of this plan?

options.A: To provide individualized steps the client should take at the first signs of a COPD exacerbation
options.B: To replace routine follow-up with the health care provider once the plan has been written
options.C: To delay contacting the health care provider until symptoms become severe enough to require emergency treatment
options.D: To keep the same response plan indefinitely without reviewing it with the health care provider

rationale: A is correct. Current American Thoracic Society patient guidance defines a COPD Action Plan as a set of instructions or steps to take at the first sign of an exacerbation. The plan may include use of prescribed rescue medication, contacting the health care provider, starting previously prescribed treatment when directed, and criteria for seeking emergency care. ATS emphasizes that each person needs an individualized plan created with the health care provider and reviewed regularly. B, C, and D contradict these principles. The source item's broader outcome claim that an action plan necessarily reduces emergency care was removed because the final construct does not require that additional causal claim.
educational_objective: Use an individualized COPD action plan to help the client recognize early exacerbation symptoms and follow predefined, provider-developed response steps, with regular review rather than replacement of clinical follow-up.
source_version_date: ATS Patient Education resource; online version updated March 2024; current resource accessed 2026-08-18
source_locator: ATS 'Exacerbation of COPD' → section 'What Is an Action Plan?': an Action Plan is a set of instructions or steps to take at the first sign of an exacerbation; it may direct rescue-inhaler use, contacting the health care provider, starting prescribed steroid/antibiotic therapy, and when to go to the emergency department; each person needs an individualized plan created with the health care provider and reviewed regularly. 'Action Steps': watch for signs and symptoms and call the health care provider promptly when symptoms begin.
source_claim_supported: Current ATS guidance directly supports individualized COPD action plans as predefined steps taken at the first sign of an exacerbation, developed with the health care provider and reviewed regularly.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Management of Care client-needs subcategory (15–21% of items), within Safe and Effective Care Environment; this item tests coordinated client education, follow-up planning, and appropriate escalation of care.
correction_summary: Substantive rebuild. The generic GOLD homepage was replaced with a current ATS COPD exacerbation resource containing an exact Action Plan section. The final item tests the directly supported purpose of individualized early-response instructions and removes the source item's unneeded causal claim about reducing emergency-care use.
audit_findings: The original GOLD root URL did not provide an exact locator for the action-plan claim.
Current ATS guidance directly defines an Action Plan as steps to take at the first sign of a COPD exacerbation.
ATS directly supports individualized provider-developed plans and regular review, excluding the distractors that replace follow-up, delay escalation, or freeze the plan indefinitely.
The unneeded claim that action plans necessarily reduce emergency-care use was removed rather than inferred from general self-management benefit.
Independent adversarial second pass found one uniquely correct answer, no second defensible option, no cueing, no unsupported medication dose or timing rule, and no unresolved conflict.
